q.t: Two half turns in the same direction make:
q.e: A full turn is the whole, and 1/2 + 1/2 = 1.

q.t: A right angle is how much of a full turn?
q.e: 4 right angles fill one full turn, so each is a quarter.

q.t: An angle smaller than a right angle is called:
q.e: Acute means smaller than a quarter turn.

q.t: An angle of exactly a half turn is called:
q.e: After a half turn the arm points the opposite way, so both arms make one straight line.

q.t: How many quarter turns make a full turn?
An angle bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle is:
q.e: Obtuse is between a quarter turn and a half turn.

q.t: The corner of a page is:
q.e: A page corner is made by two straight edges meeting squarely — a quarter turn.

q.t: The minute hand moves from 12 to 6. How much has it turned?
q.e: 6 is exactly opposite 12, halfway round the clock.

q.t: Scissors opened only a little make:
q.e: A small opening is less than a quarter turn, so it is acute.

q.t: Two quarter turns in the same direction make:
The minute hand moves from 12 to 3. How much has it turned?
q.e: 3 is a quarter of the way round the clock (15 of 60 minutes).

q.t: The minute hand moves clockwise from 12 to 9. How much has it turned?
q.e: 12 → 3 → 6 → 9 is three quarter turns.

q.t: You face the door and make a half turn. Which way do you face now?
o: The opposite way, away from the door
q.e: A half turn makes you point exactly opposite to where you started.

q.t: A turn of 2/8 is the same as:
q.e: 2/8 = 1/4 (divide top and bottom by 2) — equivalent fractions.

q.t: A turn of 3/8 makes which kind of angle?
q.e: 3/8 is more than 2/8 (a quarter) but less than 4/8 (a half).

q.t: A turn of 1/8 makes which kind of angle?
q.e: 1/8 is half of a quarter turn — smaller than a right angle.

q.t: A turn of 4/8 makes which kind of angle?
q.e: 4/8 = 1/2, which is a half turn.

q.t: How many 1/8 turns make a full turn?
q.e: A circle folded into 8 equal parts has 8 eighths.

q.t: How many quarter turns make three-quarters of a turn?
q.e: 3/4 is three lots of 1/4.

q.t: At 3 o’clock, the two hands of a clock make:
q.e: The hands point at 12 and 3 — a quarter of the way round.

q.t: At 6 o’clock, the two hands of a clock make:
q.e: 12 and 6 are exactly opposite — a half turn apart.

q.t: At 1 o’clock, the two hands of a clock make:
q.e: 12 to 1 is much less than 12 to 3, which is a right angle.

q.t: At 5 o’clock, the two hands of a clock make:
q.e: 12 to 5 is more than 12 to 3 (right angle) but less than 12 to 6 (straight).

q.t: The minute hand moves from 12 to 4. What fraction of a full turn is that?
q.e: The clock has 12 equal steps; 4 of 12 = 4/12 = 1/3.

q.t: You add two acute turns together. What do you get?
o: It can be acute or obtuse — it depends on their sizes
q.e: Two small acute turns stay acute; two large ones go past a quarter turn.

q.t: A half turn followed by a quarter turn (same direction) makes:
Sahana makes 3 quarter turns, then 1 more quarter turn the same way. Which way does she face?
o: A quarter turn away from the start
q.e: 4 quarter turns = 1 full turn, which brings her back to the start.

q.t: Two right angles put together make:
q.e: 1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, a half turn — a straight angle.

q.t: How many 1/8 turns make a right angle?
q.e: A right angle is 1/4 = 2/8.

q.t: A turn of 5/8 is:
q.e: A half turn is 4/8, and 5/8 is one eighth more.

q.t: The hour hand makes one full turn in 12 hours. How many full turns does it make in one day (24 hours)?
q.e: 24 hours is two lots of 12 hours.

q.t: How many minutes does the minute hand take to make a half turn?
q.e: A full turn takes 60 minutes, so half a turn takes 30.

q.t: Ravi turns 1/4, then 1/2, then 1/4, all in the same direction. How far has he turned in all?
Ravi turns 3/8, then another 3/8 the same way. How far has he turned?
At which time do the clock hands make an OBTUSE angle?
q.e: At 4 the hands are 4 of 12 steps apart — more than 3 (right angle), less than 6 (straight).

q.t: A wheel makes a quarter turn every second. How many full turns does it make in 1 minute?
q.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds = 60 quarter turns, and 4 quarters make a full turn: 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

q.t: How many quarter turns are there in 3 full turns?
q.e: Each full turn has 4 quarter turns: 3 × 4 = 12.

q.t: ‘Two right angles together always make a straight angle.’ Is this always, sometimes or never true?
q.e: Every right angle is exactly 1/4 turn, and 1/4 + 1/4 is always 1/2.

q.t: Rahul faces the blackboard and turns 3/4 of a turn clockwise. How much more must he turn clockwise to face the board again?
q.e: He needs a full turn in all, and 1 − 3/4 = 1/4.

q.t: On a turn-measurer folded into 8 equal parts, the arm moves 6 parts. What is that turn?
o: 3/4 turn — more than a straight angle
An obtuse angle, less than a straight angle
q.e: 6/8 = 3/4, which is more than 4/8 = a half turn.
